subtitle: The building blocks — learn these, decode everything else
notes: The most productive radicals and components, with Japanese radical names, position variants (亻 vs 人, 氵 vs 水), look-alike warnings (礻 vs 衤), and phonetic components that unlock on-reading guesses.
source: Hand-authored for Kanjido v1 (factual common-knowledge kanji composition).

cards.etymology: にんべん — 人 squeezed to the left side. The single most common radical; almost always means the kanji is about people or what people do.
ひと — two legs walking. As a component on the bottom or right it keeps this shape; on the left it becomes 亻.
おんなへん on the left. A kneeling figure in the oldest forms. Signals female, relationships, or (in older coinages) flattering/unflattering social judgments.
こ — a swaddled baby with outstretched arms. Bottom or right position. Pairs with 女 in 好 'like'.

examples.meaning: character, letter (child under a roof learning)

cards.etymology: ちから — a flexed arm. Signals effort, force, muscle.
こころ — a stylized heart. At the bottom of a kanji it means emotion or thought; squeezed to the left it becomes 忄(りっしんべん).
りっしんべん — 心 compressed to the left side. Same meaning as 心: the kanji is about an emotion or state of mind.

examples.meaning: busy (heart + dying — your heart is dying)

cards.etymology: て — five fingers on a palm. As a left-side radical it compresses to 扌(てへん).
てへん — 手 squeezed to the left. Marks hands-on actions: holding, throwing, pushing, picking up.
あし — a kneecap over a footprint. As a left radical (あしへん) it marks leg actions: run, jump, kick, step.
くち — an open mouth. Signals speaking, eating, or any opening/entrance. One of the most reused components in the whole writing system.
め — an eye turned on its side. Signals seeing and attention.
みみ — an ear in profile. Signals hearing.
ごんべん on the left — sound waves rising from a mouth. Marks the huge family of speech kanji: talk, read, language, translate, promise.
みる — an eye (目) on legs (儿): a walking eyeball. Appears on the right in observation kanji.

examples.meaning: parent (watches over you from a tree)

cards.etymology: ひ／にち — the sun with a spot in it. Top, bottom, left (ひへん) — anywhere. Signals time, light, weather.
つき — but beware: on the LEFT of body kanji it's actually にくづき, the flattened form of 肉 'meat'. 腕 arm, 腰 hip, 肝 liver — those are flesh, not moons.
き — trunk, branches, roots. As きへん on the left it marks trees, wood, and wooden things.
みず — a stream with droplets. On the left it compresses to the three splashes 氵(さんずい).
さんずい — three splashes of water down the left side. Marks liquids, seas, washing, swimming. One of the top-3 most common radicals.
ひ — flames rising. At the bottom of a kanji it flattens into four dots 灬 (れっか) — 熱 hot, 焼 grill, 点 point all carry fire.
つち — a mound of soil on the ground line. つちへん on the left marks ground, terrain, places.
やま — three peaks. Any position. Signals mountains and steepness.
かわ — three lines of flowing water. Compare 州 (sandbanks in the stream).

examples.meaning: kun reading (words flowing like a river)

cards.etymology: た — a field divided into four paddies, seen from above. Foundational in 男 'man' (power in the field) and 思 'think'.
いし — a cliff (厂) with a rock (口) at its base. いしへん marks minerals, hardness, breaking.
くさかんむり — two blades of grass across the top. Marks plants, flowers, vegetables, herbs — and by extension tea and medicine.
たけかんむり — two bamboo stalks across the top. Marks things historically made of bamboo: writing implements, boxes, counting tools.
あめかんむり — drops falling from a cloud under the sky. Tops the weather family: snow, cloud, thunder, electricity.
むし — originally a snake; now covers all creepy-crawlies. むしへん marks bugs and, oddly, the rainbow 虹.
さかな — head, scaled body, tail fin (the four dots). うおへん marks fish species — the sushi-menu radical.
とり — a long-tailed bird in profile. Compare 烏 'crow' — identical but missing the eye stroke, because crows are so black you can't see the eye.
けものへん — a dog rotated to the left side. Marks mammals and wildness: cat, monkey, fox, hunting, 'crazy'.
うま — mane flying, four legs as dots. うまへん marks horses, riding, and stations (駅 — where you changed horses).
うし — a horned head from the front. うしへん marks cattle and things done to/with them: 物 'thing' is originally a sacrificial ox.
ひつじ — horns over a woolly body. A big sheep is 美 'beautiful' — fat sheep were wealth.
かい — a cowrie shell, the oldest Chinese currency. かいへん marks money and value: buy, sell, lend, poverty, prizes.
うかんむり — a peaked roof with a chimney dot. Whatever sits under it happens indoors: 家 home, 安 peace, 字 written character.

examples.meaning: house (a pig under a roof — old farm life)

cards.etymology: まだれ — a roof with one open wall: a lean-to or public building. Marks shops, offices, wide spaces: 店, 広, 度, 庭.
やまいだれ — a bed (爿) tipped against the wall with someone on it. Everything inside is an ailment: 病 illness, 痛 pain, 疲 fatigue.
もんがまえ — double doors of a gate. What's inside the gate is the action: an ear is 聞 'hear', a mouth is 問 'ask', the sun is 間 'interval'.
くにがまえ — a closed box around the whole kanji. Marks bounded spaces: 国 country, 園 garden, 回 rotation, 困 trapped (a tree boxed in = trouble).
しんにょう — a road plus a foot, wrapped under the kanji. Whatever rides on it is going somewhere: 道 road, 近 near, 送 send, 運 carry.
Two radicals, one shape. LEFT = こざとへん, a terraced hill: 阪 slope, 防 defend, 陽 sunshine. RIGHT = おおざと, a town: 都 capital, 部 section, 郵 mail.
ぎょうにんべん — half of 行: a step with the back foot still lifted. Marks roads taken and progress made: 行く's family, 待 wait, 後 behind, 復 return.
かたな — a curved single-edged blade. On the right it compresses to 刂 (りっとう).
りっとう — 刀 standing upright on the right edge. Marks cutting and separating: 別 separate, 利 profit (cutting grain), 判 judge.
いとへん — a twisted skein of silk. Marks textiles, ties, and continuity: paper, line, connection, 'continue'.
かねへん — nuggets buried under the earth beneath a roof. Marks metals and metal objects: iron, silver, needle, bell, mirror.
こめへん — grains scattering from a stalk, 八十八 (88) overlaid — the proverbial 88 labors to grow rice. Also means 'America' in abbreviations (米国).
しょくへん — a lidded pot of cooked rice. Marks meals and feeding: 飯 cooked rice, 飲 drink, 館 a hall (where guests are fed).
くるまへん — a cart seen from above: axle through a wheel. Marks vehicles and rotation: 転 roll, 軽 light(weight), 輪 wheel/ring.
ゆみへん — an unstrung bow in profile. Marks pulling and tension: 引 pull, 強 strong, 弱 weak (two fraying bows).
ころも — a robe with draping sleeves. On the left it compresses to 衤(ころもへん) — one stroke MORE than the altar radical 礻. Mixing those two up changes 'shrine' kanji into 'shirt' kanji.

examples.meaning: first (cutting cloth for a new garment)

cards.etymology: しめすへん — compressed 示 'altar'. Marks the sacred: 神 god, 礼 courtesy, 祈 pray, 祝 celebrate. One stroke fewer than the clothes radical 衤 — count the dots.
いち — the simplest kanji and a component everywhere: a floor (上), a ceiling (下), a horizon (旦).
じゅう — a complete crossing. As a component it often just means 'needle' (the original drawing): 針 needle, 計 measure.
だい — a person with arms flung wide: 'this big!'. Component in 太 fat, 天 heaven (the line above the biggest thing), 犬 dog.
ちいさい — a thing splitting into smaller pieces. On top of a kanji it often shrinks to ⺌: 当, 光, 学's crown.
しろ — the sun 日 with a ray on top: dazzling white. Component in 百 hundred, 泊 stay overnight.
たつ — a person standing on the ground line. たつへん in 駅, 新, 親 — often hints at something established or upright.

examples.meaning: sound (standing sun? no — a tongue made visible)

cards.etymology: おう — the one who connects heaven, earth and humanity (three lines, one axis). On the LEFT it's actually 玉 'jewel' minus its dot (たまへん): 球 ball, 理 logic (carving a jewel along its veins).
こう — a carpenter's square. Marks making and work: 空 sky (a carved-out hollow), 左 left (the hand holding the tool).
また — originally a right hand. Hides in many 'doing' kanji: 友 friend (two hands clasped), 取 take, 受 receive.
すん — a hand with a pulse-point dot: the old inch, measured at the wrist. Marks precision and rules: 時 time, 寺 temple (where rules were kept).
しかばね — a slumped seated figure (politely, 'flag'). Tops 屋 shop/roof, 局 office, 居 reside — places where bodies sit.
しゃく — a hand-span: about 30 cm. Appears in 訳 translation and 駅 station (via its phonetic role).
Phonetic component reading や/ち — it lends its sound: 地 (ち) ground, 池 (ち→いけ) pond, 他 (た) other. Spotting phonetic components like this unlocks on-reading guesses.
Phonetic か — its sound carries into 何 (か→なに), 河 river, 歌 song (two 可 + yawning mouth 欠). A workhorse phonetic.
あお — life-colored: growing plants over a well. As a phonetic it gives せい/しょう to 晴 clear sky, 静 quiet, 精 refined, 情 emotion.
せい — a sprout pushing out of the ground. Component and phonetic in 星 star (sun-born), 性 nature, 姓 surname.
まい — a kneeling mother (母) with a hairpin: 'every' mother. Phonetic in 海 sea (every water) and 梅 plum.
あなかんむり — a roof over a dug-out 八: a cave dwelling. Tops 空 sky/empty, 究 research (digging to the bottom of things), 窓 window.
おおがい — a big head on legs. On the right it marks head things: 顔 face, 頭 head, 題 topic, 順 order. (Also counts pages — ページ.)
ぼくづくり／のぶん — a hand holding a stick. On the right it marks deliberate action, often forceful: 教 teach (beat knowledge in — old methods), 数 count, 政 govern.
あくび — a person with mouth wide open. On the right it marks open-mouthed actions: 歌 sing, 飲 drink, 欲 desire (gaping for more).
るまた — a hand wielding a pike. Marks destructive or constructive force on the right: 殺 kill, 段 steps, 設 establish.
ほこ — a long-handled battle axe. Lurks in 戦 war, 成 become (work completed by force), 我 I/ego (a hand gripping a weapon — the assertive self).
Phonetic component: lends ぎょう/しょう sounds and a sense of height — 焼 burn (flames rising high), 暁 daybreak.
A small cocoon of thread. Doubles in 幼 infancy and hides inside 糸, 楽, 後. Signals smallness and beginnings.
A dragging foot — walking with effort. Tops 冬 winter (the season that drags) and 各 each (arriving one by one).
ひとあし — a pair of legs under the kanji, carrying it around: 見 see (an eye on legs), 兄 older brother (a big mouth on legs), 先 ahead.
わかんむり — a cloth draped over something. Lighter than the roof 宀 (no chimney). Caps 写 copy, 軍 army, 冠 crown itself.
なべぶた — 'pot lid'. A dot and a line capping the kanji: 京 capital, 夜 night, 高 tall all wear it.
がんだれ — an overhanging cliff face. Shelters 原 meadow/origin (a spring under the cliff), 厚 thick, 歴 history.
ぼう — a person hidden away: gone. Phonetic and meaning donor to 忙 busy (heart perishing), 忘 forget (heart losing it), 望 hope (gazing after what's gone).
ひょう — a slip of paper. Strong phonetic: 標 signpost, 漂 drift (paper on water). Recognize it and you can read half the ひょう words you meet.
